candidates: When a doctest example prints output from an unordered collection (e.g. a `set`, or any structure whose repr order is not guaranteed), guard it with `# doctest: +SKIP` or restructure the example to avoid ordering sensitivity; unguarded doctests on such output will fail non-deterministically across Python versions and runs.

Iterating over `dict.keys()` is equivalent to iterating over the dict directly; flag redundant `.keys()` calls in iteration contexts (e.g. `for k in d.keys()`, `list(d.keys())`) and simplify to `for k in d` or `list(d)`.

When an `Atoms` property (or similar rich-object property) returns an object with its own documented API, include illustrative examples directly in that property's docstring — even if the returned object's class has its own docs — because users encounter the API through the property first and will not discover the full interface otherwise.

In ASE, old-style getter methods (e.g. `get_chemical_symbols()`) that duplicate functionality already available through a cleaner Pythonic property or sequence interface (e.g. `list(atoms.symbols)`) should be flagged as deprecation candidates; when reviewing code that calls such legacy getters, check whether a deprecation warning and recommended migration path should be added, allowing a suitable warning period before removal given their widespread use.
